rationale: Linear frontage: a single 16.0 x 8.5 m bar (1.88 : 1) shallow enough that every habitable room occupies a full-depth bay along one of the two long facades, so all three bedrooms, the living room, the eat-in kitchen and the office glaze directly to the outside and no room depends on borrowed light. A straight 11 m² hall runs as an uninterrupted spine along the length of the bar, entered from the middle of the north frontage; it separates the loud western third (living opening to the kitchen, kitchen near the entrance for groceries) from the quiet eastern half (parents' room and two children's rooms plus the office at the gable end). The trade-off: the bathroom is the only room pushed off the facade, sitting internally against the hall between the kitchen and the sleeping wing — it is entered from the hall and never through a bedroom, and giving up its window is what let both children's rooms and the office keep full-width exterior bays. Programme totals 105 m² against 136 m² gross, leaving about 23% for walls and the hall's own manoeuvring width, and the 16.0 m frontage sits comfortably within the 18.0 m plot while the 8.5 m depth leaves a deep south garden on the 24.0 m plot.
